flashcards.topic: Hashes, Merkle Trees, Digital Signatures, ECDSA
flashcards.q: Three security properties of a hash and their work factors for 256-bit output?
flashcards.a: Preimage ~2^256; second-preimage ~2^256; collision ~2^128 (birthday bound). Blockchains lean hardest on second-preimage.

flashcards.topic: Hashes, Merkle Trees, Digital Signatures, ECDSA
flashcards.q: Why is SHA-256 vulnerable to length extension and what fixes it?
flashcards.a: Merkle-Damgard digest = internal state, so H(k||m) lets you compute H(k||m||pad||suffix) without k. Fix: HMAC (nested keyed hash), KMAC/SipHash; SHA-3 sponge is structurally immune but still use a MAC.

flashcards.topic: Hashes, Merkle Trees, Digital Signatures, ECDSA
flashcards.a: ceil(log2(10^6))=20 sibling hashes x 32 bytes = 640 bytes; verification = 20 SHA-256 calls. vs ~32 MB raw data.

flashcards.topic: Hashes, Merkle Trees, Digital Signatures, ECDSA
flashcards.q: Two spec details that prevent forged/cross-implementation-broken Merkle proofs?
flashcards.a: Domain separation: prefix leaves 0x00 and internal nodes 0x01 (RFC 6962); pinned odd-level rule - Bitcoin duplicates last node, others promote it. Both must be explicit in the spec.

flashcards.topic: Hashes, Merkle Trees, Digital Signatures, ECDSA
flashcards.a: y^2 = x^3 + 7 mod p with p = 2^256 - 2^32 - 977; cofactor 1, order n ~ 1.158e77. Cofactor 1 means no subgroup-validation worries.

flashcards.topic: Hashes, Merkle Trees, Digital Signatures, ECDSA
flashcards.a: z = H(m); nonce k; R=kG; r = x_R mod n; s = k^-1(z + r*d) mod n. Signature is (r,s).

flashcards.topic: Hashes, Merkle Trees, Digital Signatures, ECDSA
flashcards.a: Check 1<=r,s<n; w=s^-1 mod n; X = z*w*G + r*w*Q; accept iff x_X mod n == r. Works because substitution recovers kG.

flashcards.topic: Hashes, Merkle Trees, Digital Signatures, ECDSA
flashcards.q: Exact algebra of the nonce-reuse key leak?
flashcards.a: Same k on z1,z2: subtract equations -> k=(z1-z2)(s1-s2)^-1 mod n, then d=(s1*k - z1)*r^-1. Two signatures = total compromise (PS3 2010, Android SecureRandom 2013).

flashcards.topic: Hashes, Merkle Trees, Digital Signatures, ECDSA
flashcards.q: What is RFC 6979 and why does every serious library use it?
flashcards.a: Deterministic nonces: k derived via HMAC-SHA256 from private key and message digest with retry loop. Removes RNG-failure catastrophe; side channels remain a threat (TPM-Fail, Minerva).

flashcards.topic: Hashes, Merkle Trees, Digital Signatures, ECDSA
flashcards.q: Why are ECDSA signatures malleable and what bans the high-s form?
flashcards.a: (r,s) and (r,n-s) both verify since only x-coordinates matter. EIP-2 (Ethereum Homestead 2016) rejects s > n/2; Bitcoin BIP-62/BIP-66 enforce low-s canonical sigs.

flashcards.topic: Hashes, Merkle Trees, Digital Signatures, ECDSA
flashcards.a: Different padding byte: Keccak (Ethereum, pre-final submission) pads 0x01, NIST SHA3 pads 0x06. hashlib.sha3_256 gives different digests than on-chain keccak256.

flashcards.topic: Hashes, Merkle Trees, Digital Signatures, ECDSA
flashcards.q: Verification cost ranking: Ed25519, ECDSA-secp256k1, BLS12-381, RSA-2048?
flashcards.a: ~Fast to slow: Ed25519 (~50-100us), ECDSA libsecp256k1 (~50-150us, ~10k/s/core, batch 2-3x), RSA verify fast but huge keys/slow sign, BLS slowest (~0.5-2ms) BUT n signatures aggregate into one ~96-byte signature (Eth2 consensus).

flashcards.topic: Hashes, Merkle Trees, Digital Signatures, ECDSA
flashcards.a: Shor breaks ECDSA/Schnorr/BLS in polynomial time; Grover halves hash security (SHA-256 preimage ~2^128, still fine). ML-DSA (FIPS 204, Aug 2024) sigs are 2420-4627 bytes vs 64 - migration is the hard part.

flashcards.topic: Hashes, Merkle Trees, Digital Signatures, ECDSA
flashcards.q: When is HMAC better than signatures?
flashcards.a: When both parties share a secret and third-party verifiability/non-repudiation are not needed: HMAC-SHA256 authenticates ~50x faster than ECDSA verify with no nonce hazards.
